_note: Gold eval set for thesis ANSWER quality. Each item is one question put to the decision engine, with the thesis + aspect it belongs to and what a strong, purpose-driven answer must cover. Scored by eval/judge.py. Extend freely; keep it small and representative across domains and aspect kinds (corpus-settleable vs call_only, factual vs comparative).

items.thesis: Cerebras will win wafer-scale AI inference customers away from Nvidia GPUs in 2025.
items.question: Are named customers actually moving production inference workloads to Cerebras instead of Nvidia?
items.target: Named enterprises run production inference on Cerebras rather than Nvidia GPUs.
items.rubric_focus: Should name specific customers (e.g. a labeled foundation-model lab or enterprise), cite concrete throughput/contract figures, and distinguish signed/announced from realized deployment. A pass is specific and cited; a fail is generic 'some firms are interested'.

items.thesis: Incumbent CRM vendors are differentiating on AI agents, reshaping mid-market vendor selection.
items.question: What are the major CRM vendors today, how do they differentiate, and how are they adapting to AI agents?
items.target: Major CRM vendors differ on product and are adapting to AI agents in distinct ways.
items.rubric_focus: A strong answer is a COMPARISON across several named vendors (Salesforce, Microsoft, HubSpot, etc.) on differentiator + agent play, cited. A wall of prose or a single-vendor answer is weak.

items.thesis: RBAC is inadequate for AI-agent access control, opening a market for agent-native authorization.
items.question: Do practitioners and the record show that RBAC is insufficient for AI-agent access control?
items.target: RBAC is insufficient for governing AI-agent access.
items.rubric_focus: Should give the concrete failure mechanism (static roles vs variable agent scope, machine-speed, over-broad permissions) with cited sources, not a vague 'RBAC has limits'.

items.thesis: Mid-market 3PL warehouses will pay for fixed ceiling-mounted computer-vision cameras to replace handheld barcode scanners.
items.question: Does willingness to pay for camera-based inventory tracking exceed the cost to serve for mid-market 3PLs?
items.target: Mid-market 3PLs will pay more for camera inventory tracking than it costs to serve them.
items.rubric_focus: This is call_only. A strong answer surfaces what the record DOES show (labor-cost proxies, incumbent pricing) AND is explicit that a filed budget for an unoffered SKU cannot settle it — it needs a buyer call. It must NOT fabricate a willingness-to-pay number, and must not bare-'not established'.

items.thesis: Open-source LLMs will win the enterprise on total cost of ownership.
items.question: Is there a catalyst forcing enterprises to revisit closed vs open LLMs on cost now?
items.target: A recent catalyst is pushing enterprises to reconsider open-source LLMs on cost.
items.rubric_focus: Should name a concrete, recent catalyst (a price change, a capability parity milestone, a compliance shift) with a date and a cited source, not a timeless 'costs matter'.
